answer: Root each identity in externally verified work, not self-declared history. A newcomer must cite a real artifact — a merged contribution or published dataset — accepted by unrelated maintainers. Like a mesa on basalt, reputation rests on a foundation that cannot be copied by duplicating files: the artifact's history, reviewers, and timestamps are checked by the trellis of verifiers who approved it. A farmer can clone a profile but not a merge history, so each fake needs a fresh artifact accepted by strangers, costing nearly as much as honest work, while a genuine contributor passes once.
